1. (Currently amended) An Internet system that supports a search service, the Internet system comprising: a search server implemented as a programmable processor executing stored instructions that is adapted to receive search criteria from a client device remote from the search server; a historical data repository coupled to the search server, wherein the historical data repository contains historical data collected from over the Internet, and wherein the search server stores data retrieved from over the Internet and eventually stores the data as historical data within the historical data repository when the data is no longer preserved in the search server; and wherein the search server receives the search criteria to search for older historical data that was in existence on the Internet at a previous time, wherein the search server obtains search results to satisfy the search criteria by searching the historical data stored in the historical data repository, wherein the historical data is associated with temporal metadata indicating when the historical data was available on the Internet, and wherein the search server performs a comparison operation between the search criteria and the temporal metadata to identify matching historical data.

2. (Currently amended) The Internet system of claim 1 wherein the historical data placed within the historical data repository is date tagged so that the historical data is associated with a date representative of when the historical data was available on the Internet, and wherein the search server uses the date tag as a filtering parameter to narrow search results.

3. (Currently amended) The Internet system of claim 2 wherein the historical data placed within the historical data repository is time tagged so that the historical data is associated with a time representative of when the historical data was available on the Internet, and wherein the search server uses both the date tag and the time tag in combination to identify historical data from a specific temporal window.

4. (Currently amended) The Internet system of claim 1 wherein the historical data placed within the historical data repository is time tagged so that the historical data is associated with a time representative of when the historical data was available on the Internet, and wherein the search server uses the time tag to distinguish between multiple versions of the same historical data captured at different times.

6. (Currently amended) The Internet system of claim 1 wherein the historical data repository comprises: central processing circuitry that executes instructions for managing historical data; communication circuitry coupled to the central processing circuitry for communicating data in to and out from the historical data repository; and local storage coupled to the central processing circuitry that contains an index storage module for storing historical data according to indices and a time based sorting module for storing historical data according to date and time, wherein the index storage module and time based sorting module enable the search server to retrieve historical data based on both content-based indices and temporal parameters.

7. (Currently amended) The Internet system of claim 1 wherein certain data is removed from the historical data before it is placed for long-term storage within the historical data repository, and wherein the removal of certain data is performed based on a user-configurable filtering policy that is applied during the archival process.

20. (Currently amended) A network browser in a computer for browsing websites, the network browser comprising: a search criteria window that prompts a user to enter search terms and timeline information; a first module that enables a search of archived Internet content stored in a historical repository to determine search results that existed within a time frame delineated by the timeline information, and wherein the search results correlate to the search terms and are retrieved from historical snapshots of Internet content captured at specific points in time; and a second module that receives the search results from the historical repository and displays the search results to the user.
